- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops >2%), model often lags; adjust forecast to match trend 1–2 days ahead.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by 1–2% downward to align with historical mean.  
- If true outcome deviates >5% from model in first 3 days, model is likely misaligned with sentiment; re-calibrate forecast using sentiment-weighted moving average.
